display.purpose: Hero numbers in KPI cards (total scanned count, confidence scores). Used sparingly—only for the single most important metric per card.

title.purpose: Card headers, modal titles, section labels. Always paired with an icon or visual anchor.

body.purpose: Standard UI text, descriptions, criteria lists, table content. Max line length ~80ch in long-form areas.

label.purpose: Uppercase section headers ("CORE OPERATIONS"), inline tags, and emphasis labels.

mono.purpose: All numeric values, egg IDs, FPS counters, millisecond latencies, YOLO probabilities, batch codes. Prevents number-width jitter during live updates.

shadows.name: shadow-sm
shadows.purpose: Resting state for KPI cards, table rows, input fields. Barely perceptible, exists to separate card from background.

shadows.name: shadow-md
shadows.purpose: Hover state for cards, active dropdowns, floating status pills. Signals "this is interactive."

shadows.name: shadow-lg
shadows.purpose: Modals, popovers, critical decision overlays. Reserved for surfaces that demand immediate attention.

shadows.name: glow-teal
shadows.purpose: Live indicators (pulsing dots, status pills). Glow signals real-time activity.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for card hover, button transitions, sidebar nav interactions.

motion.name: ease-bounce
motion.purpose: Modal entrance animations for attention-grabbing effect.

motion.name: pulse-dot
motion.value: @keyframes pulse-dot { 0%, 100% { transform: scale(1); opacity: 1; } 50% { transform: scale(1.4); opacity: 0.6; } }
motion.purpose: Pulsing animation for live status dots (1.8s infinite). Signals real-time system activity.

motion.name: scanline
motion.purpose: HUD-style scanline effect for camera inspection viewport (2.6s linear infinite).

components.css: .ds-hero-decision { border-radius: 12px; padding: 16px 20px; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; border: 1px solid transparent; transition: all 0.3s ease; cursor: pointer; } .ds-hero-decision.ds-grade-a { background: linear-gradient(135deg, rgba(16, 185, 129, 0.08) 0%, rgba(16, 185, 129, 0.16) 100%); border-color: #a7f3d0; } .ds-classification-meta { font-size: 0.65rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.06em; color: #64748b; margin-bottom: 2px; } .ds-grade-big-name { font-size: 1.85rem; font-weight: 800; line-height: 1.1; letter-spacing: -0.02em; color: #10b981; } .ds-grade-status-pill { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; padding: 4px 10px; border-radius: 9999px; font-size: 0.72rem; font-weight: 700; margin-top: 6px; background-color: #059669; color: #ffffff; } .ds-pill-dot { width: 5px; height: 5px; border-radius: 50%; background-color: #ffffff; } .ds-decision-right { text-align: right; } .ds-score-meta { font-size: 0.65rem; color: #64748b; font-weight: 600; } .ds-score-value { font-size: 1.55rem; font-weight: 800; color: #0f172a; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; line-height: 1.2; } .ds-yolo-prob-row { font-size: 0.68rem; color: #64748b; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; margin-top: 4px; } .ds-yolo-prob-row strong { color: #059669; margin-left: 4px; }

narrative.overview:
EggSort-AI is a real-time industrial monitoring dashboard built for precision, density, and technical clarity. The visual language prioritizes computer vision aesthetics, scientific instrumentation patterns, and the cognitive demands of continuous production monitoring. Every interface element serves operational decision-making: KPI cards display dense telemetry without clutter, status indicators pulse with live system state, and decision surfaces present algorithm confidence scores alongside visual inspection modes. The design rejects consumer softness in favor of industrial legibility—high contrast, monospaced metrics, HUD-style overlays, and grade-coded color assignments that instantly communicate product classification.

Dark sidebar navigation grounds the interface with a command-center aesthetic. The teal accent (#059669, #10b981) ties to AI/ML visual conventions and provides a distinct, non-alarming active state across live indicators, confidence rings, and actuator status badges. Layout density scales to show 4-column KPI grids, side-by-side camera inspection panels, and scrolling scan logs without compromising readability. Typography pairs geometric humanist sans (Plus Jakarta Sans) for UI labels with technical mono (JetBrains Mono) for numeric data, IDs, and timestamps.
keyCharacteristics: Data-dense layouts optimized for continuous monitoring
Live-state indicators (pulse dots, status pills, real-time badges)
Grade-coded color semantics (A = green, B = blue, Reject = red)
HUD and reticle overlays for visual inspection modes
Dark sidebar with vibrant teal active states

rules.name: The One-Accent Rule
rules.body: Teal appears only on interactive elements, live indicators, and primary actions. Decorative use dilutes its operational signal. Status pills, active nav items, and confidence scores earn the accent; static ornament does not.

rules.name: The Grade-Semantic Rule
rules.body: Green = Grade A, Blue = Grade B, Red = Reject. These assignments are strict and system-wide. No color may substitute for grade coding (e.g., no yellow warnings in grade UI). Users rely on instant color recognition during high-speed sorting.

rules.name: The Mono-for-Numbers Rule
rules.body: Any value that updates in real-time or needs horizontal alignment (counts, percentages, ms timings, coordinates) must use JetBrains Mono. Variable-width numerals cause UI layout thrash during live data streams.

rules.name: The Hierarchy-by-Weight Rule
rules.body: Size changes are minimal (0.65rem to 1.85rem span). Weight and letter-spacing create hierarchy: 800 weight + tight tracking for hero numbers, 700 weight + wide tracking for headers, 500 weight + normal spacing for body.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: Resting UI has minimal shadow (shadow-sm). Elevation appears only on interaction (hover, focus, open state). Never stack shadows for decorative depth—this is an industrial tool, not a consumer app.

rules.name: The Glow-for-Live Rule
rules.body: Live indicators (pulsing dots, status pills, active nav states) use box-shadow glow instead of elevation shadows. Glow signals real-time activity; drop-shadow signals interactive surface. Never confuse the two.

dos: Do use JetBrains Mono (0.68rem, 600 weight) for all real-time numeric values, IDs, timestamps, and API data. Variable-width numerals cause layout jitter.
Do reserve the teal accent (#059669, #10b981) for interactive elements, live indicators, and primary actions. ≤15% accent coverage per screen preserves signal strength.
Do apply grade-semantic colors (green A, blue B, red Reject) consistently across KPI cards, decision banners, confidence rings, and criteria checklists. Users rely on color = grade.
Do include pulsing status dots (7px, 0 0 6px glow, animation: pulse-dot 1.8s) on all live-state indicators. Pulse = real-time activity.
Do use shadow-sm for resting cards, shadow-md for hover, shadow-lg for modals. Elevation signals interactivity, not decoration.
Do maintain 14px radius on large cards/modals, 10px on medium containers, 6px on buttons/inputs, 9999px on status pills. Scale radius by component size.
Do set maximum content width to 1720px to support ultra-wide production monitors without excessive line lengths.
donts: Don't use teal accent for static decoration, ornamental icons, or non-interactive text. Teal = action or live state.
Don't substitute grade colors. Never use yellow/orange/purple in place of the strict green/blue/red grade triad. Industrial users depend on instant color → classification mapping.
Don't apply Plus Jakarta Sans to numeric data that updates in real-time. Use mono only. Proportional numerals (1 vs. 0) have different widths and cause UI thrash.
Don't add decorative shadows or excessive elevation. The system is functionally flat with shadows only for interaction (hover) or hierarchy (modal over content).
Don't round every corner to the same radius. Large surfaces earn 14px, small buttons get 6px, pills are infinite. Radius hierarchy clarifies component scale.
Don't exceed ~80% information density on Operate-mode dashboards. Leave 20% structural whitespace (gaps, padding) to prevent cognitive overload during 8-hour monitoring shifts.
